entry.title: [CRITICAL] Linux kernel (FIPS) vulnerabilities
entry.summary: [CRITICAL] Several security issues were discovered in the Linux kernel. An attacker could possibly use these to compromise the system. This update corrects flaws in the following subsystems: - x86 architecture; - Hardware monitoring drivers; - OCFS2 file system; - IPv4 networking; - Ethernet bridge; - Netfilter; - XFRM subsystem; (CVE-2025-21656, CVE-2026-63940, CVE-2026-74350, CVE-2026-98432, CVE-2026-99999) Ubuntu. Run apt update and apt upgrade, then reboot if the kernel changed. Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-9027-2

entry.title: [WATCH] Linux kernel (NVIDIA Tegra) vulnerabilities
entry.summary: [WATCH] It was discovered that some AMD processors did not properly perform Reverse Map Table (RMP) checks when the IOMMU accessed certain host buffers. A local attacker with hypervisor access could possibly use this to trigger an out-of-bounds condition and compromise the integrity of SEV-SNP guest memory. Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-9091-1

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Missing Initialization of a Variable Vulnerability
entry.summary: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel contains a missing initialization of a variable vulnerability that could allow for unintended modification of page-cache-backed data via failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as… Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-10-31 for US agencies). Source: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46300

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Race Condition Vulnerability
entry.summary: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel contains a race condition vulnerability which allows concurrent writes to the same AF_ALG socket causing data to be unpredictably interleaved and creating inconsistencies in the socket's internal state. Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-09-21 for US agencies). Source: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-39964

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability
entry.summary: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the ebtables SNAT target which allows an ARP sender hardware address rewrite to write directly into a nonlinear socket-buffer fragment backed by a splice-imported file page. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version. Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-09-21 for US agencies). Source: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-53266

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability
entry.summary: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel contains an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability in the TLS receive path which allows a zero-length record retrieved from the rx_list to bypass the intended recvmsg() record-type handling, potentially causing subsequent TLS records to be processed using incorrect zero-copy and queuing assumptions. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service… Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-09-21 for US agencies). Source: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-39682

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Integer Overflow Vulnerability
entry.summary: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the create_elf_tables() function which could allow an unprivileged local user with access to SUID (or otherwise privileged) binary to escalate their privileges on the system.
